title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated deepfake video and fake social media profiles to present themselves as a real, named attorney. The failure did not originate inside a single AI product deployed by a company, but in the deliberate misuse of generative tools to fabricate a credible professional identity at scale. The harm landed at the point of contact between victims and the fake accounts, before any legitimate service provider was involved at all.

The scale reported, nearly 6,500 fake profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, indicates that platform-level detection did not flag or remove the content automatically and in time. Catching this kind of abuse would have required either automated detection of synthetic video, cross-account coordination signals, or reports from the impersonated party, and here it fell to the attorney himself to hire a third-party anti-piracy firm to do the removal work.

What is not established is who the scammers are, where they operate from, or whether any platform or law enforcement body has identified them, and no legal finding has been reported.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using deepfake videos and fake social media profiles featuring his likeness to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals create fake accounts across multiple platforms and produce AI-generated videos offering immigration services that Leal has never provided, typically requesting payments of thousands of dollars through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App for services such as obtaining US residency or securing release from detention centers. The scheme escalated dramatically in recent months after Leal's office first noticed suspicious activity in October.

To combat the fraud, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scammers typically direct victims through social media videos to contact phone numbers via WhatsApp, where they exchange fake contracts and phony testimonials. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the source of the scams. He warns immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid those requesting immediate payments through digital money transfer apps.
